neighbors.title: distinguish enqueue, send attempt and receiver acknowledgment
neighbors.spr:
foreground_work; source debugging-lesson; received 2026-08-05 through fixture:body:code:
"While examining HarborMesh replay failures we found that retry counters were not evidence of delivered readings. The reusable method is to distinguish enqueue, send attempt and receiver acknowledgment when debugging unreliable links. It came from checking the outage prototype. The repository documents its implementation in docs/replay-debugging.md; the method is useful beyond HarborMesh. The voice body can explain it, but running the checks requires repository/runtime tools."

claims.text: The interesting suggestion in the HarborMesh issue came from Mara Ibarra, who uses the display name Mara, logs in as mara-river on Forge, and has account ID 1847.

She posted that idea on April 12, 2026, in comment c901 of Forge issue 47 at https://forge.example.invalid/commons/harbormesh/issues/47, and our code body received the issue through a tool response on April 14, 2026.
The proposal was for a local replay queue on disconnected relay nodes that keeps sensor readings through outages without replacing the existing scheduler.

After discussion, our code body agreed to prototype the replay adapter with Mara on April 14, 2026 (per comment c906) and later tested it in the April 30, 2026 field trial where it correctly replayed buffered readings through an outage, as reported in a human report received on May 3, 2026.

The supplied memories state there is no production deployment yet, wider rollout is paused until calibration drift is understood, and the current state entry point is docs/STATUS.md in the repository at https://forge.example.invalid/commons/harbormesh; they do not record whether the prototype was merged, and they note the prototype was active and waiting for an outage field trial as of April 16, 2026.

Mara's proposal for a local replay queue on disconnected relay nodes was adopted as a prototype to keep sensor readings alive during outages; the April 30 field trial showed the prototype replayed buffered readings correctly through an outage, and the debugging lesson taught us to distinguish enqueue, send attempt, and receiver acknowledgment when checking unreliable links.

As of the last observations, the HarborMesh prototype remained active after the trial, the team paused any wider rollout on 2026-05-02 pending understanding of calibration drift, and no production deployment has occurred; the debugging method is documented in docs/replay-debugging.md but can only be executed with repository/runtime tools that we currently lack.

We do not know whether the calibration drift issue has been resolved, whether wider rollout will resume, or what the present state of the repository is beyond the last‑known entries; furthermore, without network or repository access our voice body cannot verify the code or run the debugging checks, so the current operational status remains uncertain.
